### Study / Title
<!-- field: study.title -->
Ambispective Evaluation of the Sentinel Patch in Adults With Postoperative Pain
<!-- /field -->

### Study / Background
<!-- field: study.background -->
Postoperative pain outcomes are captured inconsistently across historical records and prospective follow-up, limiting interpretation of recovery patterns.
<!-- /field -->

### Study / Hypothesis
<!-- field: study.hypothesis -->
Combined historical records and prospective follow-up will show measurable improvement in pain tracking completeness by Month 3.
<!-- /field -->

### Study / Timeline
<!-- field: study.timeline -->
Historical record review plus prospective baseline through Month 3 follow-up, with prospective participation lasting approximately 14 weeks.
<!-- /field -->

### Population / Study Population
<!-- field: population.study_population -->
Adults 18 to 80 years old with eligible historical records and ability to complete prospective Sentinel Patch follow-up.
<!-- /field -->

### Population / Sample Size
<!-- field: population.sample_size -->
60 participants
<!-- /field -->

### Population / Sample Justification
<!-- field: population.sample_justification -->
The sample allows descriptive estimation across two sites while accounting for expected attrition and available historical records.

### Population / Inclusion Criteria
<!-- field: population.inclusion_criteria -->
- Adults 18 to 80 years old with eligible historical records and ability to complete prospective Sentinel Patch follow-up.
<!-- /field -->

### Population / Exclusion Criteria
<!-- field: population.exclusion_criteria -->
- Concurrent interventional study participation
- Incomplete historical records
- Inability to complete follow-up
- Investigator-determined safety concern
